I recall that the energy required to heat water can be calculated using the formula:
Q = mcΔT
Where Q is the energy (in Joules), m is mass (kg), c is specific heat capacity (J/kg°C), and ΔT is the change in temperature.

But since the inputs are given in cubic meters, I need to convert that to mass. 1 m³ of water is approximately 1000 kg because the density of water is about 1000 kg/m³. The specific heat capacity of water is around 4.186 kJ/kg°C.
